overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation. The chair had listed the topic on the notice and later told the public it would be discussed, so the meeting was conducted properly. The profane-comments allegation was declined as outside the statute.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the chair misled the public by saying at the start of the meeting that a recreational overlay topic would not be discussed, then allowing it to be discussed.
allegations.key_passage: we discern no error in how the Board conducted the October 11, 2017 meeting

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the chair responded to his request to speak with profane comments. The AG treated this as outside the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: this allegation, even if true, would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25. As such, we do not review it.
